questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.label: A
choices.text: outdated

choices.label: B
choices.text: lonely

choices.label: C
choices.text: forgotten

choices.label: D

questions.passage:
The following text is from Amy Tan’s 1989 novel [i]The Joy Luck Club[/i]. The narrator describes practicing the piano when she was a child.

For the talent show, I was to play a piece called ‘Pleading Child’ from Schumann’s [i]Scenes from Childhood[/i]. It was a simple, moody piece that sounded more difficult than it was. I was supposed to memorize the whole thing, playing the repeat parts twice to make the piece sound longer. But I dawdled over it, playing a few bars and then [u]cheating[/u], looking up to see what notes followed. I never really listened to what I was playing. I daydreamed about being somewhere else, about being someone else.

©1989 by Amy Tan
questions.prompt: Based on the text, when the narrator describes herself as ‘cheating,’ what does she most likely mean?

choices.label: A
choices.text: She was violating an expectation about how to perform the piece.

choices.label: B
choices.text: She was deceiving her piano teacher.

choices.label: C
choices.text: She was gaining an unfair advantage over other contestants in the talent show.

choices.label: D
choices.text: She was lying to herself about her musical ability.

explanation.short: She was supposed to play from memory but looked at the score, violating that expectation.
explanation.key_evidence: "I was supposed to memorize the whole thing" contrasts with "looking up to see what notes followed."
explanation.why_correct: The narrator explains her own use of "cheating" by immediately describing her glance at the notes. That action breaks the stated requirement to memorize the piece.
explanation.detailed: Read the disputed word together with the requirement established earlier. The expected behavior is memorization, while the actual behavior is checking the written music after a few bars. The passage does not need to establish dishonesty toward another person: the local contrast already defines the departure from the performance expectation.

choice_analysis.A: Correct. Looking at the notes instead of relying on memory violates the explicitly stated expectation for playing the piece.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. No teacher's presence, awareness, or deception is described. This adds a target of dishonesty that the text does not identify.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. The passage describes her practice habits, not an advantage she gained over other talent-show contestants.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. She admits that she dawdles and does not listen closely; she does not describe convincing herself that she has greater musical ability.

choices.label: B

choices.label: C

choices.label: D

explanation.why_correct: "Dynamic" means characterized by change or activity. The text describes precisely that quality through the delta's continual evolution and changing size and shape.
explanation.detailed: The colon introduces an explanation of the word in the blank. The repeated descriptions of evolution and changes in size and shape define the intended quality. The required adjective must therefore describe ongoing change rather than endurance, superiority, or permanence.

questions.passage:
Average Monetized Productivity Loss at Two Points After Programs Began, in Australian Dollars

| Type of training | 12 weeks | 12 months |
|---|---:|---:|
| EET | 268 | 171 |
| EHP | 282 | 436 |

Michelle Pereira et al. hypothesized that introducing health improvements into workplaces would increase productivity by reducing absenteeism (sick employees not working) and presenteeism (sick workers working less productively due to illness). Pereira's team enrolled groups of Australian workers in two programs: one that gave employees exercise training (EET) and one that enrolled employees in health promotion seminars (EHP). They then calculated the productivity loss of those groups at 12 weeks and 12 months after the programs began (based on the 28 days preceding each point). choices.label: B
choices.text: Productivity loss was largely due to absenteeism for the EHP group at 12 months after the program began, while productivity loss was largely due to presenteeism for the EET group at 12 months after the program began.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Productivity loss was consistently higher for the EHP group than for the EET group over the twelve months that it was measured, though the size of the difference between the two decreased over that time.

explanation.key_evidence: At 12 weeks EET 268/EHP 282; at 12 months EET 171/EHP 436 Australian dollars.
explanation.why_correct: The conclusion requires both a later EET advantage and time before it becomes clear. Similar initial losses followed by opposite changes support both parts.

explanation.why_correct: A accurately presents a ninefold difference, much more striking than C's true but modest comparison.
explanation.detailed: Read both the table and the lead-in Most remarkably. Numerical truth alone is not enough: A contrasts 18 million with 2 million, whereas C contrasts 4 million with 3 million. A therefore gives the strongest accurate illustration of the surprising sales gap.

choice_analysis.A: Both figures are correct and give the largest proportional and absolute contrast among the accurate choices.
choice_analysis.B: Game & Watch sold 18 million, not 4 million, and ColecoVision sold 2 million, not 3 million.
choice_analysis.C: Both figures are true, but a 4-to-3 million contrast is far less remarkable than the 18-to-2 million contrast in A.
choice_analysis.D: MSX sold 4 million, not 18 million, and Intellivision sold 3 million, not 2 million.

questions.passage: Consumers increasingly expect that goods they purchase online will be delivered rapidly, even as soon as the day of purchase. Although efficiencies in long-distance transport of parcels have greatly improved delivery times, last-mile logistics (the final step in delivery to consumers) present a bottleneck for delivery companies. Time pressure resulting from consumer expectations is not the only challenge; other obstacles, such as complex and inefficient delivery routes, persist. While innovations to mitigate these challenges have been emerging—the use of autonomous delivery robots, for instance—success has been constrained due to the additional complications that arise (e.g., robots travel relatively slowly since they must navigate many ground-level obstacles). Consequently, ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: the use of autonomous delivery robots may enable delivery companies to meet consumers' expectations now but likely is not viable as a permanent solution.

choices.label: B
choices.text: innovations in last-mile logistics seem poised to increase consumers' expectations for rapid delivery.

choices.label: C
choices.text: delivery companies should invest more funds in proven long-distance transport technologies than in untested last-mile solutions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: in the near term, delivery companies are unlikely to overcome the impediments associated with last-mile logistics.

explanation.short: The proposed innovation has limitations, so the bottleneck is likely to persist.
explanation.key_evidence: Robots travel relatively slowly because they must navigate ground-level obstacles.
explanation.why_correct: D draws a cautious near-term conclusion from the remaining obstacles.
explanation.detailed: Improved long-distance transport has not removed the final delivery bottleneck. Robots are an attempted remedy, but their additional constraints prevent the passage from treating them as a successful solution now.

choice_analysis.A: The text does not say robots already meet current expectations.
choice_analysis.B: Consumer expectations are presented as existing pressure, not as an effect of innovations.
choice_analysis.C: No cost-benefit comparison or investment recommendation is supported.
choice_analysis.D: Continuing obstacles and constrained innovations support this limited prediction.

questions.passage: Microbial fuel cells (MFCs) capitalize on the ability of some species of bacteria to metabolize metal, liberating electrons. The bacteria form a dense biofilm on the surface of an electron-collecting anode, but moving the electrons from the bacterial cytoplasm to an external electrode requires that the electrons pass through a series of inefficient oxidation-reduction (redox) reactions. Accordingly, MFC power output rarely exceeds a density of 0.30 milliwatts per square centimeter (mW/cm²). In an experiment, researchers added silver nanoparticles to carbon paper covering the anode in an MFC. The resulting power density was 0.66 mW/cm². Since metals such as silver exhibit high electrical conductivity, the researchers hypothesized that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: silver nanoparticles may increase the metabolic processes of the bacteria, thereby increasing the number of free electrons available to transfer to the electrode.

choices.label: B
choices.text: electrons may be conducted directly to the electrode before the silver nanoparticles catalyze the redox reactions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: as the density of the biofilm increases, the series of redox reactions may accelerate independent of the presence of the silver nanoparticles.

choices.label: D
choices.text: silver nanoparticles may allow electrons to bypass the series of redox reactions and transfer directly to the electrode.

explanation.short: Conductive silver offers an electron-transfer shortcut.
explanation.key_evidence: Electron transfer through inefficient redox reactions limits power output.
explanation.why_correct: D explains the higher output by allowing electrons to bypass the bottleneck.
explanation.detailed: The key causal link is conductivity. Silver could carry electrons directly to the electrode instead of requiring the inefficient sequence; this explains increased electrical output without asserting new bacterial metabolism or denser biofilm.

choice_analysis.A: No evidence indicates more metabolic activity or additional liberated electrons.
choice_analysis.B: It retains a catalytic redox explanation rather than bypassing the inefficient sequence.
choice_analysis.C: The experiment does not establish a density increase independent of silver.
choice_analysis.D: A direct conductive route explains the improvement using the property highlighted.

questions.passage: Many studies have found a positive association between levels of dissolved organic carbon and mercury in bodies of fresh water undisturbed by human activity. But Stéphane Guédron, Delphine Tisserand, and colleagues did not find this correlation in an examination of freshwater bodies impacted by wastewater, leading some scientists to hypothesize that the association could be particular to undisturbed waters. However, Ida Tjerngren and colleagues carried out a study on freshwater bodies disturbed by urban development that showed similar results to the studies on undisturbed waters, suggesting that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: the effects of wastewater on the association between levels of dissolved organic carbon and mercury should not be taken as indicative of the effects of every type of human disturbance.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Guédron, Tisserand, and colleagues’ study used different methods to measure the concentration of mercury in fresh water than Tjerngren and colleagues’ study did.

choices.label: C
choices.text: disturbances linked to wastewater affect significantly more bodies of fresh water than disturbances linked to urban development do.

choices.label: D
choices.text: levels of dissolved organic carbon and mercury are both much higher in bodies of fresh water impacted by wastewater than they are in bodies of fresh water disturbed by urban development.

explanation.short: Different human disturbances need not have the same effect.
explanation.key_evidence: Urban-development waters showed results similar to undisturbed waters.
explanation.why_correct: A limits the wastewater finding instead of generalizing it to all human disturbance.
explanation.detailed: The initial hypothesis predicts that disturbed waters lack the association. The urban-development study is a counterexample: those waters are disturbed yet retain it. The conclusion must distinguish types of disturbance.

choice_analysis.A: Wastewater cannot stand for all human disturbance because the urban result differs.
choice_analysis.B: No measurement-method comparison is supplied.
choice_analysis.C: No counts of affected freshwater bodies are compared.
choice_analysis.D: Correlation presence does not establish either group's absolute concentrations.

questions.passage: The ratio of methane to other atmospheric constituents—represented by a measure called the methane mole fraction—influences a variety of meteorological phenomena, notably precipitation and humidity. For Titan, Saturn’s largest moon, the observational data that exist are too sparse and discrepant to fully constrain the range of the methane mole fraction at various atmospheric levels. Juan Lora and colleagues point out that outputs of the IPSL atmospheric model of Titan, which track closely to observations in some respects, reflect how the model’s developers responded to this challenge: by prescribing a uniform methane mole fraction for the lowest level of the atmosphere. It is therefore important to note that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: even though the model’s outputs sometimes agree with observational data, Titan’s real methane mole fraction is likely higher than the methane mole fraction used in the model.

choices.label: B
choices.text: inconsistencies across the model’s simulations of Titan’s precipitation and humidity could be attributable to variations in the moon’s methane mole fraction.

choices.label: C
choices.text: further observations of Titan may clarify the moon’s methane mole fraction sufficiently for the model to employ a single value rather than a range.

choices.label: D
choices.text: some disagreements between the model’s simulations of Titan’s precipitation and humidity and the moon’s actual precipitation and humidity are to be expected.

explanation.short: A simplifying model assumption can limit agreement with observations.
explanation.key_evidence: The model prescribes a uniform methane mole fraction despite sparse, discrepant data.
explanation.why_correct: D predicts some model–reality differences without claiming an unsupported direction.
explanation.detailed: Methane affects precipitation and humidity. Because its observed distribution is poorly constrained, developers impose uniformity. That simplification can cause model outputs to diverge from actual weather even when some outputs match observations.

choice_analysis.A: Nothing establishes that the real fraction must be higher rather than lower.
choice_analysis.B: The described uniform input does not itself explain variation among the model's simulations.
choice_analysis.C: The model already uses a uniform value; the choice reverses the issue.
choice_analysis.D: Some differences from actual weather are consistent with the stated simplification.

questions.passage: Cy Twombly, a US painter and sculptor, created many large-scale abstract works, such as his 10-painting series [i]Fifty Days at Iliam[/i]. In these works, Twombly’s artistic style is exemplified by his use of graffiti-like ______ often incorporate words or phrases from poetry and mythology.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.label: A
choices.text: scribbles; that

choices.label: B
choices.text: scribbles that

choices.label: C
choices.text: scribbles: that

choices.label: D
choices.text: scribbles. That

explanation.short: Keep the defining relative clause attached to scribbles.
explanation.key_evidence: scribbles that often incorporate words or phrases
explanation.why_correct: B forms a single noun phrase whose relative clause identifies the scribbles.
explanation.detailed: The main sentence already has a subject and verb. The remaining words describe the noun scribbles; they are not a new independent sentence. No semicolon, colon, or period should split that noun from its that-clause.

choice_analysis.A: A semicolon cannot introduce this dependent relative clause.
choice_analysis.B: No punctuation interrupts the noun and its defining relative clause.
choice_analysis.C: A colon unnecessarily breaks the noun from its modifier.
choice_analysis.D: The period leaves That often incorporate without an independent main clause.

questions.passage: The 2020 documentary [i]Without a Whisper—Konnon:Kwe[/i] was directed by Katsitsionni Fox. It explores how Indigenous Haudenosaunee culture shaped the woman suffrage movement in the early nineteenth ______ how the personal and political authority Haudenosaunee women had in their communities influenced the first suffragists in the US.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.label: A
choices.text: century. Revealing

choices.label: B
choices.text: century; revealing

choices.label: C
choices.text: century, revealing

choices.label: D
choices.text: century revealing

explanation.short: Use a comma before the supplementary revealing phrase.
explanation.key_evidence: It explores how ... culture shaped the woman suffrage movement ... , revealing how ...
explanation.why_correct: C attaches the nonfinite explanation to a complete preceding clause.
explanation.detailed: Revealing does not introduce another independent clause: it has no finite main verb or separate subject. The comma presents it as supplementary information about the film's exploration.

choice_analysis.A: A period would leave a Revealing fragment.
choice_analysis.B: A semicolon requires an independent clause on both sides.
choice_analysis.C: A comma correctly introduces the supplementary participial phrase.
choice_analysis.D: Without a comma, revealing is improperly run into the completed time phrase.

questions.passage: Mitochondrial genomes reproduce asexually, which should over time result in an accumulation of harmful mutations and a decline in mitochondrial functionality. However, nuclear genes are hypothesized to coevolve with the rate of mitochondrial decline, eliminating mutational erosion. Such a compensatory measure ______ the organelle’s decline, unlike enzyme-stabilizing accessory proteins, offers an evolutionary explanation of mitochondrial reproduction.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.label: A
choices.text: counteracting

choices.label: B
choices.text: counteracted

choices.label: C
choices.text: had counteracted

choices.label: D
choices.text: counteracts

explanation.short: Counteracting modifies measure; offers is the main finite verb.
explanation.key_evidence: Such a compensatory measure counteracting the organelle's decline ... offers an explanation.
explanation.why_correct: A adds a participial modifier without creating a second unconnected predicate.
explanation.detailed: Restore the source's single blank after measure. The core is measure offers an explanation. Counteracting the organelle's decline describes the measure. The other choices introduce finite verbs before offers without a coordinator or relative pronoun.

choice_analysis.A: Counteracting correctly forms an active participial modifier of measure.
choice_analysis.B: Counteracted takes decline as its object and creates an unconnected finite predicate before offers.
choice_analysis.C: Had counteracted similarly creates a second finite verb phrase without a clause connection.
choice_analysis.D: Counteracts would compete with offers as an unconnected finite predicate.

questions.passage: In the list ‘Things That Make One’s Heart Beat Faster’ from Sei Shonagon’s [i]Pillow Book[/i], the author delights in a cloudy mirror, rain on a window, and scented robes. So shrewd an observer is Shonagon, a lady-in-waiting to Empress Teishi, that her book’s musings on tenth-century Japanese courtly life ______ readers a thousand years later.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.label: A
choices.text: fascinate

choices.label: B
choices.text: has fascinated

choices.label: C
choices.text: is fascinating

choices.label: D
choices.text: fascinates

explanation.short: Musings is plural, so fascinate supplies the agreeing verb.
explanation.key_evidence: her book's musings ... fascinate readers a thousand years later
explanation.why_correct: A agrees with the plural subject musings, not singular book.
explanation.detailed: The possessive book's identifies whose musings they are; it does not determine verb number. Remove the intervening phrase on tenth-century Japanese courtly life to see the core musings fascinate readers.

choice_analysis.A: Fascinate is the finite present form agreeing with plural musings.
choice_analysis.B: Has fascinated uses singular has with a plural subject.
choice_analysis.C: Is fascinating uses singular is with plural musings.
choice_analysis.D: Fascinates is a singular present form and disagrees with musings.

questions.passage: As an anti-federalist, Pennsylvania politician and writer Samuel Bryan objected to the US Constitution’s provisions for a powerful centralized government and opposed the document’s ratification; ______ essays he published in the [i]Philadelphia Independent Gazetteer[/i] in October 1787 under the pseudonym ‘Centinel’ disparaged the arguments of the federalists, who supported the Constitution’s adoption.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: by comparison,

choices.label: B
choices.text: fittingly,

choices.label: C
choices.text: nevertheless,

choices.label: D
choices.text: in other words,

explanation.short: The essays are fitting conduct for an anti-federalist.
explanation.key_evidence: Bryan opposed ratification, and his essays disparaged arguments for adoption.
explanation.why_correct: B marks the expected consistency between his stance and the essays.
explanation.detailed: The first clause establishes Bryan's position against a powerful centralized government and ratification. His essays then attack the federalist case for adoption. Fittingly connects this action to that established stance; it does not present a surprise or merely restate the same fact.

choice_analysis.A: No two comparable cases are being set against each other.
choice_analysis.B: Fittingly signals that the essays accord with his anti-federalist views.
choice_analysis.C: Nevertheless would suggest an unexpected contradiction, but the action matches his position.
choice_analysis.D: In other words would treat the essays as a rephrasing of the stance rather than a fitting action.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Hina Hanta is an online archive curated by the Choctaw Nation of Oklahoma.
• It features images of cultural artifacts relevant to the history of the Choctaw people.
• It features household items, including a stamp (isht inchunwa in Choctaw) made from rubber.
• The stamp was made in the 1800s.
• Hina Hanta features sports apparel, including a stickball collar (innuchi) made from horsehair.
• The stickball collar was made in 2016.
questions.prompt: The student wants to make a generalization about the Hina Hanta archive. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Choctaw name for the rubber stamp is isht inchunwa.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Included in the Hina Hanta online archive is a rubber stamp.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Not all artifacts in the Hina Hanta archive are from the 1800s.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The horsehair stickball collar (innuchi) was made in 2016.

explanation.short: Use the recent artifact to make a claim about the archive as a whole.
explanation.key_evidence: The archive includes an 1800s stamp and a collar made in 2016.
explanation.why_correct: C generalizes beyond a single object: not every item comes from the 1800s.
explanation.detailed: One 2016 item is sufficient to disprove a claim that all archived artifacts are from the 1800s. This limited generalization is supported without claiming that every period is represented.

choice_analysis.A: A translation of one object's name is not a generalization.
choice_analysis.B: The presence of one stamp is an isolated fact.
choice_analysis.C: The 2016 item supports the limited claim about the archive's range.
choice_analysis.D: It describes the collar only, rather than generalizing about the archive.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Digital Light Synthesis (DLS) is a form of additive manufacturing that utilizes light to rapidly cure liquid resin into high-quality, 3D objects.
• Step 1: Ultraviolet (UV) light images are projected up into a pool of liquid resin, where the object's first layer takes shape.
• Step 2: The partially cured resin object is raised, leaving a thin space (a "dead zone") beneath it for oxygen and liquid resin to flow through.
• Step 3: The UV light passes through the dead zone—maintaining the flow of resin—and partially cures additional layers of the object.
• Step 4: When the resin object is complete, it is baked in an oven to complete the curing.
questions.prompt: The student wants to describe how DLS cures 3D objects. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: DLS cures 3D objects by passing through a "dead zone," adding layers to the object, then curing the object in an oven.

choices.label: B
choices.text: In DLS, UV light is projected into layers of liquid resin until the resin solidifies and passes through a "dead zone," wherein the curing is completed.

choices.label: C
choices.text: In DLS, UV light images are projected into a liquid resin pool to cure a 3D object layer by layer; once solidified, the object is baked in an oven.

choices.label: D
choices.text: DLS is a form of additive manufacturing that creates a "dead zone" in which UV light solidifies layer by layer before being baked in an oven, creating a high-quality, 3D object.

explanation.short: Light cures resin layer by layer; baking completes the process.
explanation.key_evidence: UV light passes through the dead zone and partially cures additional layers.
explanation.why_correct: C preserves the roles of UV light, liquid resin, and the oven in order.
explanation.detailed: The light is projected into resin to build the object. The object, not the light, is subsequently baked. The dead zone maintains flow during construction rather than completing the cure.

choice_analysis.A: The DLS process itself is not an object passing through the dead zone.
choice_analysis.B: The dead zone does not complete curing; oven baking is the final step.
choice_analysis.C: It gives both the layer-building step and the final baking step.
choice_analysis.D: UV light does not solidify into layers or get baked.
